title: Enriched chain homotopies agree in ordinary localization
statement: Let $\mathcal N$ be a complete and cocomplete category enriched, tensored and cotensored over unbounded cochain complexes of abelian groups, with the complex adjunctions and ordinary morphisms given by degree-zero cycles as in [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model]. Suppose $\mathcal N$ has a model structure with functorial factorizations and satisfies the enriched model axiom: for a cofibration $A\to B$ and a fibration $U\to V$, the map $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(B,U)\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,U)\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,V)}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(B,V)$ is degreewise surjective and is a quasi-isomorphism if either given map is a weak equivalence. Cofibrant means that the initial map is a cofibration. Let $W$ be the weak equivalences and $\gamma:\mathcal N\to\mathcal N[W^{-1}]$ the ordinary localization, in universes where it exists. If $X$ is cofibrant, $Y$ is arbitrary, $a,b\in Z^0\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,Y)$, and $t\in\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,Y)^{-1}$ satisfies $dt=b-a$, then $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$. Thus $\gamma$ restricted to cofibrant objects factors through the category with the same objects and morphisms $H^0\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,Y)$, with composition induced by enriched composition. In particular, if $X,Y$ are cofibrant, closed degree-zero maps $a:X\to Y$, $b:Y\to X$ and degree-minus-one elements $s,t$ satisfy $ds=ba-1_X$ and $dt=ab-1_Y$, then $\gamma(a)$ and $\gamma(b)$ are mutually inverse isomorphisms. No fibrancy assumption on $X$ or $Y$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-chain-interval-tensor-cylinder] to the given $\mathcal N$ and cofibrant $X$. Its assumptions are precisely the completeness, cocompleteness, complex enrichment/tensor/cotensor adjunctions, functorial model factorizations and enriched model axiom in the present statement; no local presentability or cofibrant-generation hypothesis is needed. Obtain $J$ with $dh=e_1-e_0$, maps $i_0,i_1:X\to J\otimes X$, and a weak equivalence $p_X:J\otimes X\to X$ with $p_Xi_0=p_Xi_1=1_X$. We only use these endpoint and weak-equivalence properties of its good cylinder.

source.place: Paragraph 2, extracted mapping-complex foundation: apply the existing integral chain interval cylinder lemma.

proof.text: Put $C=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,Y)$. Define the graded group map $\phi:J\to C$ by $\phi(e_0)=a$, $\phi(e_1)=b$, and $\phi(h)=t$, zero on the other degrees. It is a chain map: on $e_0,e_1$ this is $da=db=0$, and on $h$ this is $dt=b-a=\phi(dh)$. The complex tensor-Hom adjunction and the identification of ordinary maps with degree-zero cycles in [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model] turn this chain map into an ordinary map $H:J\otimes X\to Y$. Naturality of this adjunction in $j_i:\mathbf Z[0]\to J$ identifies $Hi_i$ with $\phi j_i$, hence with $a$ for $i=0$ and $b$ for $i=1$. Only the stated enrichment conventions of that node are used, not its diagram-model theorem or its extra hypotheses.

source.place: Paragraph 2, agent expansion of enriched chain homotopy: transpose the explicit three-generator chain map through the tensor-Hom adjunction.

proof.text: Since $p_X$ is a weak equivalence, $\gamma(p_X)$ is invertible by the defining property of the localization. Applying $\gamma$ to $p_Xi_i=1_X$ and composing on the left by $\gamma(p_X)^{-1}$ gives $\gamma(i_0)=\gamma(p_X)^{-1}=\gamma(i_1)$. Therefore $\gamma(a)=\gamma(H)\gamma(i_0)=\gamma(H)\gamma(i_1)=\gamma(b)$. This is a cancellation with an invertible arrow, and uses no fibrancy of $Y$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, agent expansion: cancel the inverted cylinder projection using its two sections.

proof.text: For cofibrant objects define a category $\mathcal K$ with the same objects and morphisms $H^0\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,Y)=Z^0C/d(C^{-1})$. Composition of cycles is a cycle. It descends to these quotients: for closed degree-zero $f,g$ and degree-minus-one $u,v$ of the appropriate types, the chain-map composition rule of [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model] gives $g\,du=d(gu)$ and $(dv)f=d(vf)$. Thus changing either representative by a boundary changes its composite by a boundary. Associativity and identities descend from enriched composition. Define $\bar\gamma(X)=\gamma(X)$ and $\bar\gamma([f])=\gamma(f)$. Two representatives of the same class differ by $dt$ for some degree-minus-one $t$, so the equality already proved makes this well-defined. Functoriality is the functoriality of $\gamma$ on representatives, and $\gamma$ restricted to cofibrant objects equals $\bar\gamma$ composed with the zero-cycle quotient functor.

source.place: Paragraph 2, agent expansion: the elementary degree-zero cohomology quotient and the descended localization functor.

proof.text: Finally apply the equality just proved to the two closed endomorphisms $1_X,ba$ and the degree-minus-one $s$ with $ds=ba-1_X$; the source $X$ is cofibrant. It gives $\gamma(b)\gamma(a)=1_{\gamma X}$. Apply it again to $1_Y,ab$ and $t$ with $dt=ab-1_Y$; here the source $Y$ is cofibrant. It gives $\gamma(a)\gamma(b)=1_{\gamma Y}$. These are exactly the two inverse equations. Neither application requires a fibrant target.

source.place: Paragraph 2, agent expansion: specialize the equality to the two homotopy inverse equations.
